hints: Focus on where the nitrogen in nitrogen oxides really comes from in an engine, air or fuel?
Remember that catalytic converters are designed to remove nitrogen oxides by turning them into harmless nitrogen gas, not to make more of them.
Think about which pollutant helps oxidise sulfur dioxide in the air and which type of combustion produces the hydrocarbons needed for PAN.
walkthrough:
**Where does NO2 come from?**

Think first about the source. In an engine the very high temperature lets nitrogen and oxygen from the air react together, not impurities in the fuel.

$$\text{N}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO} \text{ then } 2\text{NO} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2$$

**What does NO2 do in the atmosphere?**

$\text{NO}_2$ can oxidise $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$, which then forms acid rain. It is regenerated afterwards, so it acts as a catalyst.

$$\text{SO}_2 + \text{NO}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_3 + \text{NO}$$
$$\text{NO} + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{NO}_2$$

**Check the other pollution stories**

A catalytic converter reduces nitrogen oxides to harmless $\text{N}_2$, it does not make $\text{NO}$ from $\text{NO}_2$. PAN (peroxyacetyl nitrate) needs unburnt hydrocarbons from incomplete combustion, not $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ from complete combustion.

$$2\text{NO} + 2\text{CO} \rightarrow \text{N}_2 + 2\text{CO}_2$$

**Conclusion**

Only the catalytic oxidation of sulfur dioxide correctly describes the chemistry of $\text{NO}_2$ in the air.

options.A: Correct. Nitrogen dioxide oxidises sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide and is itself reduced to nitrogen monoxide, which is then re-oxidised by oxygen back to nitrogen dioxide. Because it is regenerated, it acts as a catalyst in acid rain formation.
options.B: Incorrect. This reverses the job of the catalytic converter. Converters use catalysts like rhodium to reduce nitrogen oxides (NO and NO2) to harmless nitrogen, for example 2NO + 2CO gives N2 + 2CO2. They do not produce NO from NO2.
options.C: Incorrect. PAN is a photochemical smog pollutant formed when nitrogen oxides react with unburnt hydrocarbons and partially oxidised organics. Complete combustion gives only CO2 and H2O, which cannot form PAN. The trap is confusing complete with incomplete combustion.
options.D: Incorrect. Nitrogen oxides form from N2 and O2 in the air at the very high temperature (not pressure alone) in the engine. Impurities in fuel containing sulfur give SO2, and nitrogen impurities could give some NOx, but the main source of NO and NO2 is the air itself.
